original_question: Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant delta, and suppose the set K^+(f) of points with bounded forward orbit has a connected interior component U. If a convergent subsequence of iterates of f on U converges to g: U -> C^2, with rank r equal to 0 or 1 when |delta| < 1 and equal to 2 when |delta| = 1, can U be a wandering component? If so, what ranks of g can occur, and can U be bounded, unbounded of finite volume, or unbounded of infinite volume?
target_in_paper: §4, "Stable regions for complex Hénon type maps" (Milnor), Question 1: the question asking whether a connected component U of int(K^+(f)) can be wandering, and if so what ranks of the limit map g and what size/volume types of U can occur. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it has the right ambient space (C^2), the right class of maps (polynomial diffeomorphisms), the Jacobian determinant δ, the set K^+(f) of points with bounded forward orbit, a connected interior component U, a convergent subsequence of iterates on U with limit g, the rank alternatives r=0 or 1 when |δ|<1 and r=2 when |δ|=1, and the three geometric possibilities for U (bounded, unbounded of finite volume, unbounded of infinite volume). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))
missing_details: The paper first assumes that K^+(f) has non-empty interior, and only then lets U be a connected component of that interior; making the non-emptiness of int(K^+(f)) explicit restores the exact setup. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))

The nearby context explicitly says that, according to Montel, the iterates of f restricted to U possess a convergent subsequence; adding this source of convergence makes the question fully paper-faithful. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))

The official question immediately adds the necessary consequence: if U is wandering, then one must have |δ|<1. Your draft implies the dissipative case through the rank discussion, but the paper states this condition as part of the question itself. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))

The paper phrases the volume alternatives exactly as possibilities for U itself: bounded, unbounded of finite volume, or unbounded of infinite volume. Tightening to that wording makes the question maximally stand-alone and faithful. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))
refined_question: Let f be a polynomial diffeomorphism of C^2 with Jacobian determinant δ, and suppose that K^+(f):={z∈C^2 : {f^n(z)}_{n≥0} is bounded} has non-empty interior. Let U be a connected component of int(K^+(f)). By Montel, the family of iterates {f^n|_U} has a locally uniformly convergent subsequence f^{n_j}|_U→g:U→C^2. If |δ|<1, the rank r of g is 0 or 1, while if |δ|=1, r=2. Can U be a wandering component? If so, necessarily |δ|<1; in that case, can the limit map g occur with rank 0 or with rank 1, and can such a wandering U be bounded, unbounded of finite volume, or unbounded of infinite volume? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/9201271))
justification: arXiv:math/9201271 is the 1990 "Conformal dynamics problem list," not a paper with numbered items such as Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3. The draft clearly targets §4, "Stable regions for complex Hénon type maps" (Milnor), specifically Question 1 on the PDF’s p. 9, whose wording is already close to your draft. The refined version therefore stays narrow and only restores the exact setup and phrasing supplied by the paper: int(K^+(f)) is assumed non-empty, U is a connected component of that interior, Montel gives the convergent subsequence of iterates, and the paper explicitly notes that wandering would force |δ|<1. The paper does not state an equivalent reformulation of this question. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9201271))
